senses.def: special importance or attention given to something
ex: The course places emphasis on speaking.
Inversion adds emphasis and a formal tone.

mistake.wrong: He emphasized on the importance of practice.
mistake.right: He emphasized the importance of practice. / He put emphasis on the importance of practice.
mistake.note: The verb emphasize has no preposition. The noun emphasis takes on.

senses.def: [U] knowledge or skill that you get from doing a job or activity
ex: An internship helps you gain experience.
Do you have any experience of working with children?
She has ten years' experience in marketing.

senses.def: [C] something that happens to you that affects how you feel
ex: Living abroad was an amazing experience.
We had some strange experiences on that trip.

mistake.wrong: I have three years experiences in sales.
mistake.right: I have three years' experience in sales.
mistake.note: When it means خبرة, experience is uncountable. Use the plural only for تجارب (events).

senses.def: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving details
ex: Can you explain this rule to me?
He explained why he was late.

mistake.right: Can you explain this to me?
mistake.note: explain + thing + to + person. Never explain me.
